scope: Read-only product coverage review of current repository during v47 preparation. Counts describe source at review time, not independently tested live browser behavior. This artifact does not approve academic mappings.
method: Read production UI and pure engines, current source catalogs, ready-template registry and service boundaries.
Trace principal links and state transitions by code; do not infer completeness from directory or marketing counts.
Separate implemented workflows from coverage gaps and production-operational evidence.

summary.mainFinding: Most requested workflow primitives exist; consistency, discoverability and verified mapping coverage are the main gaps. Build one cohesive student journey before adding more feature surfaces.

priorityFixes.problem: What-if and savings still relabel named university coursework as missing course research and append generic approval wording to published matches.
priorityFixes.proposedChange: Use actual selected course completeness and specific conditional/personal research states. Show published placements without blanket reapproval gates.
acceptance: Fresh WGU69/41 and Liberty83/37 have zero invented missing-course warnings across compare and savings.
An actual conditional or unmatched personal course retains a precise exception.

priorityFixes.problem: The current WGU catalog202605 is not a valid outcome catalogYear and Sheet uses a year-range default instead.
priorityFixes.proposedChange: Support valid YYYYMM alongside academic years/ranges end to end, preserving exact source catalog as the default.
acceptance: A202605 outcome cannot verify a2026-2027 or another monthly catalog.

priorityFixes.problem: Main portal bypasses prior-credit and military questions; military opportunities remain hidden in course preferences.
priorityFixes.proposedChange: Offer a compact clear course-history step and optional military intake from main setup/Myplan, without requiring transcripts to generate a provisional plan.
acceptance: Startingfromzero does not produce prior-record homework.
A veteran can choose JST/CCAF before the plan checklist is generated.
An exact school/degree path remains short.

priorityFixes.problem: Signed-in students may assume local worksheet changes update their account but account copies require manual consented save.
priorityFixes.proposedChange: Make account-save state and a direct update action visible from the workspace; preserve explicit consent and conflict checks.
acceptance: A signed-in change clearly indicates device-only or account saved.
A stale revision never overwrites another device silently.

priorityFixes.problem: All38full requirement ledgers are called ready-to-use even though many have limited reviewed outside options and missing policies.
priorityFixes.proposedChange: Use plan-specific evidence and optimized outside coverage in the selection card; keep a full requirement plan distinct from a thoroughly researched accelerated route.
acceptance: A school-wide ceiling is not displayed as usable planned transfer.
A heavily conditional route does not read like verified WGU69.
Students can request another degree directly from an empty result.

features.currentBehavior: A separate public explainer site routes to the portal and course browser.
acceptanceCriteria: Home makes one primary start action available on mobile and desktop.
All public navigation reaches a useful page and private portal pages stay outside the sitemap.

features.currentBehavior: Guides, journal posts, school/source profiles, canonical URLs, structured metadata, sitemap and robots rules are generated.
acceptanceCriteria: SEO pages distinguish researched policy examples from a personalized executable plan.
Changing official domain updates canonical/sitemap/OAuth settings together.

features.currentBehavior: 38full requirement ledgers are presented across4schools; this does not establish complete outside-transfer coverage or verified policies for all38.
acceptanceCriteria: A plan card discloses actual outside-course coverage and unresolved policy conditions.
No degree with missing requirement choices is advertised as ready.
Ready templates expand by reviewed curriculum/version/format, not by degree title alone.

features.currentBehavior: 1630official listing entries and1122opportunity entries exist, but most are directory research rather than usable plans.
acceptanceCriteria: A student can request an unsupported degree using its official URL without replacing a usable active plan.
Directory-only entries never become executable recommendations or claim course equivalencies.

features.currentBehavior: Students can browse, filter, save, edit and mark courses in progress/finished without choosing a degree, then compare degree fits.
acceptanceCriteria: Saving a course does not award completed credit.
Find degree fits uses the entire private collection and preserves original provider credits/units.
Removing a saved record updates fit without silently altering unrelated records.

features.currentBehavior: 31provider profiles are available, while the merged executable course browser has354listings from6providers;114listings have unknown original credits/units.
acceptanceCriteria: Provider directory count is never shown as mapped provider coverage.
Each course differentiates source credit quantity from receiving-school award.
Add additional providers only through reviewed identities, actual receiving maps and course-level conditions.

features.currentBehavior: The main portal exposes target/explore/course-first starts, school and degree choices plus a compact goal/level/subject/format/priority form. It bypasses several detailed Journey questions.
acceptanceCriteria: Known-degree students can open that exact plan with a short setup.
New students explicitly choose no past credits versus add records later.
A student can revise goals without losing current courses, notes or previous plan versions.

features.currentBehavior: Career intent, online/campus preferences and cost/speed priority affect recommendations. Budget/study hours/exam preferences mostly live in legacy wizard or advanced controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Main consumer flow exposes only the few inputs that change recommendations.
Optional details remain discoverable from My plan with understandable labels.
A missing study pace is an optional estimate input, not missing school policy.

features.currentBehavior: JST/CCAF and military policy/checklist logic exist, but the main portal never renders its Journey military steps. Entry is buried in Course preferences.
acceptanceCriteria: An active-duty/veteran/reserve learner can identify service status from the main setup.
CCAF versus JST selection changes the records action without converting training into awarded credit.
Military benefits and residency exceptions remain sourced and eligibility-specific.

features.currentBehavior: Protected teacher/lawyer/pilot/health goals influence eligibility and add professional-entry checks; the app does not model all jurisdictional licensing requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: A general degree recommendation is not labeled a complete licensed-career route.
Jurisdiction/program-accreditation uncertainty remains specific and does not disappear when a student chooses speed.

features.currentBehavior: The default plan groups named course rows into university-specific requirement sections, with expandable details and an optional detailed worksheet.
acceptanceCriteria: A first-time student sees course, provider, requirement and credits without opening advanced tools.
General education, foundational/core, major, cognate/concentration, electives and noncourse obligations follow the actual degree.
Shared requirements count once in the degree total.

features.currentBehavior: Red/yellow/green progress comes from missing/not-started, in-progress and finished records. Degree totals distinguish finished versus school-confirmed credits.
acceptanceCriteria: Named university courses can become in progress and finished even without an outside alternative.
No school approval is inferred from saving a course or checking a generic task.
Changing the degree recomputes the same course records against the new ledger.

features.currentBehavior: Private plan-scoped tasks support statuses, due dates, notes and custom tasks; completion-sensitive steps reopen after academic changes.
acceptanceCriteria: A returning student sees one meaningful next action.
Known published policies do not become generic school-reapproval homework.
Private tasks persist across plan switches and cannot manufacture academic credit.

features.currentBehavior: The solver respects residency, upper-level rules, source action deduplication, grades and conditional placements. Only a subset of models has strong reviewed provider maps and exact policy evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Every recommended action belongs to a degree requirement and an allowed source.
The solver never maximizes raw transfer credits at the expense of residency or source-credit limits.
Course/version/format-specific evidence is required before promoting conditional maps.

features.currentBehavior: Students compare up to3routes using the same completed/in-progress/saved pool, see individual placements, save versions and switch plans with history preservation.
acceptanceCriteria: The same source course cannot earn duplicate awards across multiple requirements without an explicit reviewed bundle.
Changing school preserves source records and separates unused/potential/finished credits.
Known university coursework is not called missing source research.

features.currentBehavior: Seven published comparison models and a persistent savings strip exist, plus remaining-cost estimates and per-plan quotes/pace. Some real degree models have no comparable savings model and hide the strip in simple view.
acceptanceCriteria: The strip remains useful when tuition is known but personal pace/fees are missing.
Savings are explicitly tuition plus modeled outside costs; unknown fees are not zero.
Named university courses are not labeled missing research in savings details.
Subscription term count and completion time are separate assumptions.

features.currentBehavior: Public browsing plus signed-in posts, plan sharing, likes, upvotes, contextual comments/replies, reports, soft deletion and moderation are implemented.
acceptanceCriteria: Students can discuss a specific plan/course/school in context without leaving their private records exposed.
Public plan preview excludes completed/in-progress records and private notes.
Reports and moderation remain available on user-generated content.

features.currentBehavior: Ready catalog templates and reviewed community templates can be browsed and copied; research is reused rather than always regenerated.
acceptanceCriteria: Copying a template preserves the current course collection.
Unreviewed forum posts remain distinct from approved reusable templates.
A published revision is immutable enough for evidence to stay attached to its exact scope.

features.currentBehavior: Outcome reports and moderated proof-based badges exist. Current community catalog identifier validation accepts years/ranges only, while WGU uses a monthly catalog identifier.
acceptanceCriteria: Exact program/course/catalog scope is preserved for semester-year and monthly catalog IDs.
Two different recent moderator-reviewed positive outcomes with proof are needed for Community verified.
Conflicting recent reports downgrade the badge; votes alone do not verify academic transfer.

features.currentBehavior: A single degree URL can resolve existing source plans or start bounded server-side Claude research with status, recovery and reuse. Quality gates reject incomplete plans; arbitrary universities cannot be guaranteed a complete answer.
acceptanceCriteria: A previously reviewed degree opens without paid AI research.
A new request shows honest progress and survives interrupted networking.
Incomplete source research is owned by DegreePath and cannot be marketed as a fully loaded plan.
Program/catalog/format differences do not share incorrect cached results.

features.currentBehavior: A student can create/import a requirement ledger, edit source-bound options and save a private curriculum without waiting for a curated template.
acceptanceCriteria: Blank and CSV paths explain required columns and preview the exact credit ledger.
An imported requirement is not treated as a completed course or a reviewed university equivalency.
Replacing the active degree preserves prior versions and private records.

features.currentBehavior: A headers-only CSV download has column definitions and numbered example rows; preview occurs before adding records.
acceptanceCriteria: The template has stable columns and no example credits that could be imported as real coursework.
Invalid units/status/date/credit rows are shown before import.
Duplicate records and edits do not silently duplicate earned credits.

features.currentBehavior: Email/Google, password reset, private account plan copies, conflict-aware restore and deletion exist. Device edits do not automatically update the account copy.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in student understands whether changes are saved locally or to the account.
Cross-device continuation is reachable without guessing a hidden manual-save workflow.
Autosave, if added, is explicit consent with revision conflict protection and no loss of private records.

features.currentBehavior: Owner/admin research review, encrypted AI connection management, verified college teams and consented student information requests exist. Lead purchasing/billing is not implemented.
acceptanceCriteria: Only authorized admins publish reviewed templates.
Verified institution membership is separate from platform administration.
Colleges see only opt-in contact fields; course records and plans are not bundled into leads.
Student withdrawal blocks future access and is reflected in college views.

features.currentBehavior: Ten schools have source-linked pros/tradeoffs/accreditation/tuition/community perspectives; comparable transfer limits can be ranked. There is no submitted structured rating aggregation for ease/speed/cost/recognition.
acceptanceCriteria: Policy comparisons use like-for-like credits and source scope.
Externally sourced anecdotes are not fabricated DegreePath reviews.
Review scores require real ratings, count/date/scope and moderation before a composite ranking is shown.

features.currentBehavior: Private milestones celebrate actual saved choices and finished/accepted records; no public competitive leagues, scoring or leaderboards are implemented.
acceptanceCriteria: Milestones reflect actual records and can be corrected after data changes.
A social competition feature is not required to complete a degree or encourage unverified rushing.

features.currentBehavior: Static reviewed data, D1 schemas, indexes, auth boundaries and bounded research exist. A monthly institutional review operation, production load test, SLO/observability and backup/restore exercise are not established by code alone.
acceptanceCriteria: Each publish verifies source/compiler consistency and protects private API boundaries.
A scheduled review queue identifies stale facts without silently promoting updated data.
Measured production load and recovery tests precede any claim of readiness for millions.

intentionallyNotAdded: Fabricated student reviews, rankings or outcomes.
New public leaderboards before clear educational purpose and privacy design.
Unverified course awards or universal automatic degree plans for every university.
Payments/lead billing before institutional demand and explicit commercial terms.
releaseRecommendation: First deploy the current known-facts cleanup. Next correct comparison and savings consistency, exact community catalog identity, visible personal intake and account-save clarity; keep broad academic mapping expansion as a sourced data program rather than a UI completeness claim.

followUpReview.note: Baseline feature classification is preserved. Cohesion and correctness fixes do not imply complete institutional mapping coverage.
